title: Unit and conversion conventions used across both bases

parameters.name: M0
parameters.provenance_class: HISTORICAL-PUBLISHED-VALUE (not a default, startup value or therapy limit)

time_convention: Basis A continuous time in minutes; Basis B discrete time index t with Ts = 5 min.
measured_vs_latent: n/a
inference_notes: 18.0 mg/dL per mmol/L follows from M0=5.55556 mmol/g; the clinical paired values are consistent to rounding (70/3.9=17.9, 140/8.0=17.5). Use 18.0 only as the sourced rounding; do not mix with other factors inside one model.
gaps: Pompa writes M_wG units as [g/mol] but leaves its value implicit in M0.
implementer_verification_duties: Unit-test every interface (CGM mg/dL vs mmol/L, pump U/h vs U per cycle vs mU/min) with dimensional assertions.

statements.text: Glucose mass/concentration: G[mmol/L] = Q1[mmol] / V_G[L]  (Basis A).

Carbohydrate to glucose-equivalent: D = (1000/M_wG) d(t) (Pompa eq 173); Pompa Table 3 lists M0 = 5.55556 with printed unit 'mmol/min'; numerically M0 = 1000/180 mmol per g, i.e. M_wG = 180 g/mol (INFERENCE: unit-label misprint). If d is a rate [g/min], D is [mmol/min]; if D(t) is an amount at time t (Wilinska), it is [mmol] entering as an impulse.
INFERENCE: 1 mmol/L glucose = 18.0 mg/dL from molecular mass 180 g/mol. Murphy 2011 reports 5.8 mmol/L = 104.4 mg/dL. This is a rounded unit conversion, not a fitted parameter.

Insulin: Basis A inputs are in mU/min (Paoletti eq 18; Pompa u_basal 6.68 mU/min); Basis B inputs are U per sample period (Copp Sec 2.1). 1 U = 1000 mU is the SI milli prefix (definitional, not a modelling assumption).
Basis B per-sample basal: u_BASAL[U/h] * Ts[min] / (60 min/h) gives U per sample (Copp eq 5; Gondhalekar eq 7).

Basis A insulin input is a rate [mU/min], with boluses as mass impulses [mU] into S1. Basis B input is an amount per sample [U], relative to basal. A constant 1 U/h corresponds to 1000/60 mU/min and delivers Ts/60 U during a Ts-minute sample.

inference_notes: Wilinska 2010 appendix prints EGP = EGP0[1 + x3]; Pompa (165), Reenberg (7a) and Paoletti (15) give EGP0(1 - x3). INFERENCE: '+' is a typesetting error because x3 is described as the insulin effect that suppresses EGP.

Pompa EGP0 = 0.161*BW mmol/min (= 161 umol/kg/min) is ~10x the Cambridge population mean 16.9 umol/kg/min and Jacobs 0.0158*BW; INFERENCE: a dropped zero (0.0161*BW). Do not use 0.161 without independent confirmation.

gaps: Exercise terms (Paoletti eq 19-21) are extensions; excluded from the core physiology.
implementer_verification_duties: Assert EGP >= 0 clamp and non-negative masses; test fasting steady state at a stated target.

statements.text: dQ1/dt = -F01c - F_R - x1*Q1 + k12*Q2 + EGP + U_G
G = Q1/V_G

EGP = EGP0*(1 - x3), set to 0 when negative (Wilinska 'if EGP >= 0, 0 otherwise'). Wilinska prints [1 + x3]; INFERENCE: sign typo, corrected form printed by Pompa, Paoletti, Reenberg, Freil, Rashid (no registered erratum).
EGP0 (Hovorka 2004 restatement) = 0.0161*BW mmol/min (16.1 umol kg^-1 min^-1); Pompa's printed 0.161*BW is an inferred dropped-zero misprint (CLM-PUB-MATH-0017, CLM-PUB-MATH-REVIEW-0002).

Nonnegativity: with nonnegative inputs and parameters, the exact dynamics keep S1, S2, I, x_i, Q1, Q2, D1, D2 >= 0 (at each zero boundary the derivative is >= 0; at Q1 = 0 the Q1 outflows vanish while EGP >= 0 and k12 Q2 >= 0). Discrete integrators need not preserve this: G >= 0 and nonnegative masses must hold numerically; F01c forms are defined for G >= 0.

Variant Cambridge-simulator (Wilinska 2010): F01c = F01s*G/(G + 1.0), F01s = F01/0.85 ; F_R = R_cl*(G - R_thr)*V_G if G >= R_thr else 0.
Both renal forms are zero below threshold; F_R >= 0 above threshold requires R_cl >= 0 (a negative R_cl would reverse renal flux and add glucose).
Truncation/resampling rule for the printed R_cl prior (34% negative mass): not stated; implementer-owned.

source_locators.locator: Table 3 'Determined' rows and I0 = U_I0/(k_e V_I)

inference_notes: Because u_b = k_e V_I I_b and EGP0, S_IE, F01 enter one scalar balance, a user's basal rate constrains only a combination of parameters (identifiability; see EQ-PUB-MATH-0015).

implementer_verification_duties: Test that initialization with the user's basal reproduces a declared fasting glucose; if not, record which parameter absorbs the discrepancy.

statements.text: Method (Paoletti): choose target fasting G*, solve F(x0, u_b, D=0) = 0 for x0 and basal u_b (numerical root finding).
INFERENCE (algebra of EQ-0002/0004/0005 with D=0): I_b = u_b/(k_e V_I); x_i,b = S_i I_b; Q1,b = V_G G*; Q2,b = x1,b Q1,b/(k12 + x2,b);
0 = EGP0(1 - S_IE I_b) - F01c(G*) - F_R(G*) - x1,b Q1,b x2,b/(k12 + x2,b)   (one scalar equation in I_b).
Feasibility screen used by Paoletti after Jacobs: steady-state BG > 300 mg/dL with zero insulin; < 100 mg/dL at 15 U/h.

Startup with UNKNOWN prior boluses/temporary rates: basal steady state is an assumption, not an observation. Options: retained delivery history, or explicit initial-state uncertainty with no above-basal insulin until the history covers the action time scale. These only avoid adding insulin on an unverified assumption; neither is a safety guarantee (CLM-PUB-MATH-REVIEW-0005).

Region assumptions for statement 2: valid where S_IE I_b <= 1 (EGP clamp inactive; beyond it EGP = 0 in the balance); F01c(G*) and F_R(G*) evaluated on the branch containing G* (CHK-01: G* = 5 mmol/L, so F01c = F01, F_R = 0). No numeric bounds are implied.

initialization_steady_state: Interior-point start must be strictly feasible.
measured_vs_latent: n/a
inference_notes: INFERENCE: the glucose instance uses the non-quadratic convex output cost c^2 and hard constraints, so Thm 2 does not directly certify a saddle point; the maximizer faces a convex term in x (EQ-0019). The paper only states weights 'can be tuned ... to ensure that there exists a saddle-point'.
Recursions (17a)-(18d) were checked against the rendered PDF page 5 image (signs as written above); (18d) is [[lam_n C'C - A'P_{t-L+1}A, -A'P_{t-L+1}D],[-D'P_{t-L+1}A, lam_d I - D'P_{t-L+1}D]] > 0.
gaps: No saddle-point proof for the exact glucose instance; no warm-start or failure-fallback rule.
implementer_verification_duties: Numerically check min-max = max-min (duality gap) on recorded scenarios; define deterministic fallback on solver failure; multi-start tests.

statements.text: Assumption (Automatica Assumption 1): min-max has a saddle point (min and max commute).

Linear-quadratic sufficient conditions (ACC 2016 Thm 2): M_k = Q + A^T M_{k+1} Lambda_k^-1 A, M_{t+T} = Q; Lambda_k = I + (BB^T/lam_u - DD^T/lam_d) M_{k+1}; P_j = A^T P_{j+1} A + A^T P_{j+1} D Z_j^-1 D^T P_{j+1} A - lam_n C^T C; P_t = M_t - lam_n C^T C; Z_j = lam_d I - D^T P_{j+1} D; require (18a) lam_u I + B^T M B > 0, (18b) lam_d I - D^T M D > 0, (18c) lam_d I - D^T P D > 0, (18d) block matrix > 0. Corollary: observable system => lam_n, lam_d large enough suffice.

Solver: primal-dual interior-point Newton method on the coupled first-order conditions (dissertation Algorithms 4.3.1/4.4.2); termination at epsilon-saddle; correct when cost convex in minimizer and concave in maximizer; otherwise 'run several instances ... with random initial conditions'.

INFERENCE (sampled diagnostic, not proof): for the published instance with all window samples and X = R^3, a Hessian bound from grid-sampled curvature of c^2 is negative definite at the evaluated u_TDI points (CHK-05). A saddle point would follow (Sion) only if the bound held globally, which is not established. Evaluated points are not thresholds. Runtime duality-gap checks remain required; any modification needs re-verification (CLM-PUB-MATH-REVIEW-0007).
